facts.text: Plainfield was founded in 1761 by 56 proprietors from Plainfield, Connecticut, who invested in the New Hampshire Grants after the French and Indian War.
The Plainfield Historical Society, organized in 1978, works to collect artifacts, preserve historic structures, and share the town’s story with future generations.
In 1910, Ernest Harold Baynes founded the Meriden Bird Club, the first of its type in the nation, in Plainfield.
Kimball Union Academy, a private preparatory school, was established in 1813 on the site of Meriden Parish, named after Governor Jonathan Belcher’s farm.
Actress Ethel Barrymore spent her summers in Plainfield, New Hampshire, in the early 20th century, adding a touch of theatrical history to the town.
Plainfield hosts the Helen Woodruff Smith Bird Sanctuary and the Annie Duncan State Forest, offering residents and visitors a chance to explore diverse wildlife habitats.
